key_insight: A k-space recurrent neural network (KOSTAL) can reconstruct cardiac MRI cine images much faster than traditional gridding while preserving image quality for interventional use.
clinical_relevance: This approach could enable lower-latency, real-time cardiac MRI guidance during procedures by producing usable images from far fewer radial spokes.
method: Uses a per-coil k-space convGRU with mask-conditioned view sharing
Adds an image-space recurrent module for temporal reconstruction
Trained on open-access OCMR data and tested on prospective pediatric free-breathing scans without retraining
evidence_signal: At 10 spokes per frame, KOSTAL achieved median SSIM 0.907 and reconstructed frames in under 34 ms, outperforming gridding and maintaining strong agreement with reference cine data.
watch_item: Performance was shown on simulated and specific prospective datasets, so broader generalization and workflow integration still need validation across scanners, patients, and procedure types.
paper_title: K-space Optimized Spatial Temporal Architecture for Low Latency in Interventional Cardiac MRI
